issues.description: Class name 'PerljsonmaybexsConan' is not proper PascalCase. code_style rule #2 requires class name in format '{SoftwareName}Conan' with PascalCase. The package name 'perl-json-maybexs' has word segments separated by hyphens (perl, json, maybexs); each should be capitalized: 'PerlJsonMaybexsConan'.
issues.fix_suggestion: Rename the class to 'PerlJsonMaybexsConan' to properly capitalize each word segment from the package name.

issues.description: Class name 'PerljsonmaybexsTestConan' is not proper PascalCase. code_style rule #2 requires PascalCase format. Should be 'PerlJsonMaybexsTestConan' with each word segment capitalized.

issues.description: Shell script uses 'set -eu' but is missing '-o pipefail'. code_style rule #7 requires all scripts to use 'set -euo pipefail' for safe mode. Without pipefail, pipeline failures (e.g., grep in a pipe) can be silently swallowed.
issues.fix_suggestion: Change 'set -eu' to 'set -euo pipefail'. If the script must use #!/bin/sh (POSIX), consider switching to #!/bin/bash for pipefail support, or add explicit error checking for each pipeline.

issues.description: '|| true' used on the find command without an explicit inline comment explaining why the error is suppressed. code_style rule #10 requires a comment on the same line as '|| true' usage. While the context is clear (find returns non-zero when no files match, handled by the subsequent [ -z ] check), the rule mandates an inline comment.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add an inline comment: PM_FILE=$(find "$PERL_LIB" -name "MaybeXS.pm" -print -quit 2>/dev/null || true)  # find exits non-zero if no match; checked below

issues.description: Output format uses 'OK:'/'ERROR:' instead of the '[ok]'/'[fail]' tags specified in code_style rule #9. While this is a test_package consumer script rather than a CI build script, using standardized output tags improves consistency and parseability.
issues.fix_suggestion: Consider using '[ok]' for success messages and '[fail]' for failure messages with 8-space indentation, e.g.: echo '        [ok] Found MaybeXS.pm at $PM_FILE'

issues.description: build_system value 'perl-extutils-makemaker' is not in the standard list (cmake | autotools | makefile | meson) defined in code_style rule #14. While more descriptive for a Perl module, CI tooling may expect standard values. The build section already uses 'system: makefile' which is standard.
issues.fix_suggestion: Consider using 'makefile' as the top-level build_system value (since ExtUtils::MakeMaker generates a Makefile) and keep the Perl-specific details in comments or knowledge_gained section.
